newsitem.title: CROATIA: Privredna Banka to swap tourist assets with state.
newsitem.headline: Privredna Banka to swap tourist assets with state.

text.p: Croatia's ailing Privredna Banka said on Monday it was in the process of swapping assets in tourist firms nominally worth some 56 million German marks ($36.8 million) with the state privatisation agency.
"We hope the deal will be finalised this month," bank official Josip Protega told Reuters by telephone.
This was expected to improve management and efficiency of hotelier firms, while also helping the banks' results as the tourist trade recovered, the bank said in a newsletter.
Privredna said it would gain a controlling 64.41 percent stake in Dalmatian hotelier HTP Primosten and 53.91 percent in one of the country's main tour operators Atlas.

It would also increase its holdings in five other seaside groups -- Hoteli Jelsa to over 48 percent, Dubrovnik's Argentina to 33.25, Istrian Plava Laguna to 32.67 percent, Suncani Hvar to 30.92 and Laguna Novigrad to 22.07 percent.
In exchange, the bank would transfer to the Croatian Privatisation Fund minority stakes in seaside hoteliers, mostly on the southern Adriatic coast.
In a similar 100 million marks swap in August, another bank Zagrebacka Banka increased its share in Jadranturist to 51 percent and Istraturist to 42.7 percent.

It followed a strategic government decision aimed at enabling commercial banks to increase their shareholdings in the tourist sector they have supported for years. The banks are also expected to reap some of its rich future profits.

Privredna, which is due for a radical overhaul before the end of 1996, suffered a net loss of 570 million kuna (over $100 million) in the past two years because of huge provisions for loan losses during the war in former Yugoslavia.
The bank services most of Croatia's troubled public sector enterprises, including the steel mill Zeljezara Sisak, oil utility INA and state railway company.
But it said it hoped to at least break even if not revert to full profitability this year. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 1.52 German Marks)
